proof_review: Bracketing supplies consecutive primes p≤x<q≤P with q prime. Old1550 source gives q−p≤1550, hence x<q≤x+1550. Every ε>0 then gives q<x+1550+ε; no unsupported strict1550 assertion or fixed+1 endpoint loss.
For11≤x≤exp42 the same bracketing has p≥11: otherwise prime11 would lie strictly between p and q, contradicting consecutivity. p≤x≤exp42<4e18 establishes the exact lower-prime source domain.
log p≤log x and0≤log p imply log²p≤log²x; q−p<log²p then yields q<x+log²x. This is uniform over all real x, including prime and integer boundaries.
log²x≤W iff x≤exp√W uses x≥1,W≥0 to justify the square/root/log operations and both directions. No out-of-domain convention is used.
The minimum-width theorem selects the witness from the smaller of1550+ε andlog²x by a real comparison; it does not incorrectly require one witness to satisfy unrelated bounds.
